observations.note: Output-level watermarking families (green-list/KGW, Gumbel/EXP, distortion-free, ECC multi-bit, semantic, post-hoc substitution, certified) are all named.
Model watermarking and fingerprinting (weight-space, backdoor/instructional, EaaS, behaviour-space) covered.
Attack landscape (stealing/spoofing, scrubbing, inhibition, radioactivity, speculative sampling) covered.
Multimodal/cross-modal coverage is effectively absent: the subsection is leaked citation-check notes plus an uncited paragraph.
Code watermarking, publicly verifiable/detectable schemes, dataset/data watermarking and standard benchmarks (e.g., MarkMyWords) are missing or only named.

anchor_justification: Main pillars are present so it is generally comprehensive (3); level 4 needs only very minor omissions, but multimodal, code and data watermarking are key sub-areas that are missing or empty.

observations.note: Declared locus taxonomy is actually used to organize chapters 3-5.
Threat-model taxonomy is presented twice with the same axes (near-duplicate subsections).
Evaluation gaps treated in three chapters; equity in 6.4 and 7.3.
Leaked refinement notes and a full repeated 'corrected' version of each subsection break the flow.
Conclusion begins 'This subsection synthesizes'; transitions are formulaic.

anchor_justification: Overall ordering is reasonable and most content is orderly, matching 3 which explicitly allows repeated subsections; not 4 because transitions are rigid and two subsections are locally disordered with duplicated text.

observations.note: Content stays on watermarking/fingerprinting of LLMs.
Legal/governance rhetoric (EU AI Act articles, Daubert, UNESCO) with little technical link.
Leaked meta-notes about the survey's own citation list are unrelated to the topic.
Framing against safety/privacy/alignment is appropriate.

anchor_justification: Mostly on topic with infrequent digressions (4); not 5 because the leaked meta-notes and governance padding do not contribute to understanding the topic.

observations.note: A three-axis framework (locus, detection modality, security property) is proposed and referenced in later chapters.
'Convergence is mathematically precise' product-space KL and 'risk-proportional embedding constraint' are asserted, not derived from cited work.
Radioactivity as both defence and attack surface is a genuine cross-study theme.
Lineages between methods (e.g., WaterMod refining end-to-end differentiable watermarking) are claimed without support; flagged for Module B.

anchor_justification: Identifies thematic relationships (3) but the unifying framework is largely rhetorical; level 4 requires most studies synthesized into coherent themes, while many paragraphs are lists of methods with asserted links.

observations.note: White-box schemes infeasible for closed APIs — reasoned limitation.
Spectral fingerprints vs INT4 quantization; backdoor schemes need training control and are exposed to key leakage.
Critiques evaluation practice (synthetic perturbations, missing composite attacks) with some reasoning.
Inconsistent: rejection sampling said to 'resolve' an impossibility result that §5.4 calls information-theoretically inevitable.
Same longitudinal-decay gap restated ~7 times; most 'future work must' passages are generic.

anchor_justification: Sporadic critical evaluations, shallow or inconsistent (3); level 4 requires systematic critique of most key studies, which is absent.
